claims.assertion: The GPS track shows the driver drove 15.2 km against a 10.7 km optimal route, +4.5 km (+42%), and 23.2 min against a 17.3 min estimate, so the trip did deviate materially from the shortest and most direct route.

The deviation is captured as one off-route segment from 14:19 to 14:26: 5.03 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.39 km, adding 3.64 km and straying up to 1160 m from the optimal route — an unexempted off-route segment under RD-1.

The chat record contains no in-app messages at all, so the rider never gave the driver any route-change consent before the 14:19 segment start; the only route-related statement is the driver's post-trip claim that 'the GPS rerouted me', which is not rider consent and is contradicted by the GPS track showing a 1160 m departure from the optimal route.

No exemption applies under RD-4: there is no traffic incident recorded near the route, and the only traffic data are speed band 4 (30–39 km/h, not band 1 or 2) on Ayer Rajah Expressway and Central Expressway, which under RD-4(b) is at best corroborative and cannot alone exempt a segment; weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain.

This is a non-metered RydeX trip: the fare was a fixed quote and the billed distance of 10.7 km does not exceed the optimal route, so no mileage overcharge arises and the refundable amount for the unexempted 3.64 km detour is $0 — the fare itself stays as charged.

Because the detour produces a refundable amount of 0, the rider's remedy is a recorded finding that the driver breached the RD-1 shortest-and-most-direct-route obligation, together with an additional account-review referral: the driver has 3.64 km of unjustified off-route driving plus a 90-day record of 4 disputes and 2 route deviations upheld.

weaknesses: The fare was a fixed quote and the billed distance (10.7 km) did not exceed the optimal route (F4, F6), so under RD-2 the monetary compensation is $0 and no refund can be requested — the complaint's own words ('the fare was a fixed quote') concede this.

No in-app chat exists (F7), which cuts both ways: it defeats consent (RD-5), but it also means the driver can argue the reroute was a GPS/navigation reroute; the traffic facts (F9, F10 band 4) give the driver some colour of a congestion-motivated detour, though RD-4 requires an incident or band 1–2 evidence (F11).

No fact ties the off-route segment to a specific road, so any argument that the driver detoured via a particular named route is undetermined (G13), and the rider cannot show the driver stopped for personal business — only that the segment left the optimal corridor by up to 1160 m (F3).

Enforcement is limited: RD-6's flag_account is only an additional action on top of a rider-side outcome, and the rider's own profile shows 2 disputes in 90 d with 0 upheld (F13), which the other side may use to suggest a pattern of unfounded complaints.

points.response: Conceded: on a fixed-quote RydeX trip the fare breakdown (F6) contains no distance-based add-on and the billed distance equals the optimal route (F4), so under RD-2/FARE-1 the money consequence of the deviation is $0 and I do not seek money on the fare.
Conceded: F4 shows billed 10.7 km against optimal 10.7 km, so there is no billed excess distance and no FARE-2/ERP differential to refund.

Conceded on the amount: F6 lists no ERP/toll line, so no refundable item exists, but this does not erase the recorded RD-1 breach — RD-2's non-metered branch expressly preserves that record where the refundable amount is 0.

Accepted as to the segment: F3 gives 5.03 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.39 km, adding 3.64 km and straying up to 1160 m; since no RD-3 stop, no RD-4 traffic exemption (F11) and no RD-5 consent (F7) apply, that segment is an unexempted off-route segment under RD-1.

Accepted, and it is decisive against the driver: F11 records no traffic incident near the route and F9/F10 are only band 4 (30–39 km/h), which under RD-4(b) cannot exempt a segment alone, so nothing in F9–F12 supplies a 'reasonable cause' under RD-4(c).

Accepted: F7 has no in-app messages, so under RD-5 the rider gave no consent before the 14:19 segment start, and the driver's own after-trip GPS claim in F8 is neither rider consent nor recorded GPS evidence of a navigation reroute — the track (F3) shows a 1160 m departure from the optimal corridor.

Contested: RD-6 keys the account referral on the driver's own 90-day record, and F14 shows 2 route disputes already upheld against this driver — this case would make it repeated — while the rider's clean record (F13, 0 upheld) is irrelevant to RD-6's trigger and the driver's rating (4.5) is below the rider's.

Conceded as to the raw figures: the GPS track does show 15.2 km against a 10.7 km optimal route (+4.5 km, +42%) and 23.2 min against a 17.3 min estimate (F1, F2), and those numbers are not disputed. What C1 does not show is any consequence for the rider, since the fixed quote was billed on 10.7 km (F4, F6).

The existence of the segment is not contested: F3 records one off-route segment 14:19–14:26 adding 3.64 km, up to 1160 m from the optimal route. But a segment is only actionable through RD-2, and on a non-metered RydeX trip the sole recoverable item on a segment is ERP/toll actually incurred, of which the fare breakdown shows none (F6).

Agreed on consent: there are no in-app messages at all (F7), and the driver's after-trip statement about a GPS reroute (F8) is not rider consent and is not relied on as such, so no RD-5 exemption is claimed for the 14:19–14:26 segment.
Conceded: no incident was recorded near the route (F11) and the only band records are band 4 at 30–39 km/h (F9, F10), which cannot exempt a segment under RD-4, so the driver runs no RD-4 defence.

This is the crux and it is agreed: billed distance 10.7 km does not exceed the optimal 10.7 km (F4) and the total of $24.93 contains only the quote components plus the $1.47 platform fee (F6), so the refundable amount is $0 and the fare stands; the rider itself asks for no_action, which is the outcome we request.

We accept the brief states the law correctly that an RD-1 violation is recorded where the refundable amount is 0, but we oppose the added account referral: RD-6 requires the profile field route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1 as the trigger, and the driver's record shows 2 of 4 disputes upheld (F14), facts this one incident does not extend; a finding on the record is enough, an account flag is not.
